subject: MerchantX capacity request — temporary allocation & sign-by terms
messages:
From: Kate Holden <kate@merchantx.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@merchantx.com; procurement@merchantx.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask & timing (MerchantX)

Hi Monica,

Quick note from the MerchantX infra/ops team — we're ramping a pilot to 15M inference requests/day starting mid-June. We ran a throughput test with a comparable model and estimate we need ~4 A100-equivalent GPUs for low-latency bursts and an additional 8 GPUs for sustained throughput if traffic keeps growing.

We'd like to lock in a dedicated pool that becomes active 2027-06-01. Procurement is working toward a PO but they told us approvals could slip into late June. Can Redwood provide:
- A short-term temporary reservation that gives us capacity on 6/1 while procurement finishes?
- A clear commitment window and cancellation/preemption policy (we can't have total service loss in our checkout flows).
- Pricing for 6- and 12-month reserved commitments.

Attaching our traffic estimates and a rough ramp plan. Happy to hop on a call today if that helps.

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Holden
VP Engineering, MerchantX

Attachment: merchantx_traffic_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Kate Holden <kate@merchantx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask & timing (MerchantX)

Kate — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. We can support MerchantX's pilot but there are a couple of operational constraints I want to be transparent about up front.

High level proposal:
- Temporary allocation: 4 GPU nodes (A100-equivalent) reserved and enabled 2027-06-01 for pilot traffic (canary + production split).
- Conditional full reserve: Expand to 12 GPUs once signed SOW and PO received; target start of full capacity 2027-07-01 if paperwork complete.
- Sign-by requirement: To keep the temporary allocation in place after 2027-07-15 we need a signed 6- or 12-month SOW (deposit terms apply). Without that, we might have to retract temporary pool if capacity contention rises.

Next steps proposed:
1) I will loop in infra for a feasibility check and explicit preemption/fallback plan.
2) Sales/legal to confirm provisional pricing and deposit terms.
3) Schedule a 30-min alignment call today or tomorrow.

If that sounds OK I'll initiate the internal request now.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask & timing (MerchantX) — need decision on temporary pool

Forwarding MerchantX request and proposed short-term allocation.

Team — MerchantX is asking for a 4-node temporary allocation starting 6/1 (see attached spreadsheet). They have high growth potential and are pushing for a canary on 6/1 while procurement catches up.

Key constraints to consider:
- We have a scheduled Q3 onboarding (two other mid-enterprise deals) with committed Reserved pools in our current capacity plan.
- If we grant temporary dedicated nodes without a signed SOW, we risk having to preempt them if a higher-priority deal with signed PO needs capacity.

Requested:
- Vivek: can infra commit to a 4-node temporary pool that can be preempted under defined conditions? If so, what's the exact preemption policy we should propose to MerchantX (grace periods, warm caches, KV snapshotting, routing to hosted fallback models)?
- Karthik/Laura: confirm revenue/commit signals for MX (what's the expected ARR and legal timeline?) so infra can prioritize if we have contention.

I put Marissa on the loop for renewal/priority context.

— Monica

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask & timing (MerchantX) — need decision on temporary pool

Monica — thanks for flagging. Quick infra read: we can provision a 4-node A100-equivalent dedicated pool on 2027-06-01 with the following guardrails.

Proposed temporary-allocation policy (summary):
- Guarantee window: temporary pool is "best-effort reserved" from 2027-06-01 to 2027-07-15. Not SLA-backed.
- Continuation condition: to convert to a guaranteed reserve after 2027-07-15, we require either a signed SOW + PO OR a deposit equal to one month's committed spend.
- Preemption rules: if a higher-priority customer with a signed PO needs the exact nodes, we will trigger preemption with 72 hours notice; during that window we will provide routing to hosted fallbacks + warm KV transfer.
- Canary policy: produce a canary deployment for 48 hours (traffic capped) before opening full traffic. We will capture KV snapshots and enable prefix caching to minimize cold-start regressions.
- Auto-burst: allow best-effort burst to shared burst pool up to 20% of sustained capacity; this is not guaranteed during peak continental events.

Operational steps for Sales/Ops alignment:
1) Sales must submit HubSpot deal ID and expected ARR.
2) Infra will raise a temporary allocation ticket with the ops-on-call and tag the nodes as "preemptible-temp-MX".
3) If preemption occurs, we will coordinate with the CS lead for migration and provide credits for downtime per existing policy.

I'll attach a short memo detailing the resource fit and current utilization across our US fleet. Note: granting many of these temporary pools this quarter will increase the probability of contention in mid-June; we should be conservative on granting multiple such requests at once.

— Vivek
Director, Serving Infrastructure

Attachment: capacity_memo_infra.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask & timing (MerchantX) — need decision on temporary pool

Vivek / team — MerchantX is projecting $420k ARR if they go 12 months with the projected usage; procurement says they're "very likely" but need a few weeks. We're willing to offer an interim commercial path:

Commercial proposal for temporary window:
- Temporary allocation fee: one-time deposit equal to 20% of the first-month committed spend (protects infra against last-minute pullouts).
- Pricing: 12-month SOW gets a 28% discount off list; 6-month SOW gets 18% discount.
- If they sign the 12-month SOW by 2027-07-15 we convert the temp pool to guaranteed capacity and refund the deposit pro-rata into month 1.

If infra can accept Vivek's preemption + 72-hour notice policy, I can present this to Kate as a trade-off: near-term availability in exchange for a sign-by date.

I recommend we also attach a short "surge-expectations" doc that explains what happens to latency and KV-cache during a preemption. That will help reduce churn risk.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Kate Holden <kate@merchantx.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask & timing (MerchantX) — temporary allocation & sign-by terms

Kate — thanks again for the spreadsheet and patience while we aligned internally. Short summary and next steps so we have the decision in writing: 

1) Temporary allocation (what we can enable on 2027-06-01):
   - A 4-node A100-equivalent dedicated pool will be provisioned and available 2027-06-01. This is intended to support your pilot canary + limited production traffic.

2) Continuation & sign-by terms:
   - To avoid preemption after 2027-07-15 MerchantX must either: (a) sign a 6- or 12-month SOW and provide the PO, or (b) provide a deposit equal to one month of committed spend. If neither is received by 2027-07-15 the temporary pool becomes subject to preemption under our contention policy.

3) Preemption policy (operational summary):
   - 72 hours notice before nodes are reclaimed. During the notice window we will: provide routing to hosted fallback endpoints, export and hand off KV snapshots, and coordinate a warm-up window for caches. We will issue a credit for any sustained downtime consistent with our outage credit policy.

4) Commercial proposal:
   - If MerchantX signs a 12-month SOW by 2027-07-15 we will convert the pool to guaranteed capacity and apply a 28% discount; a 6-month SOW gets 18% discount. A deposit paid now will be applied pro-rata to month 1 of the SOW.

5) Next steps:
   - I've attached a short temporary SOW (redwood_temp_sow_v1.pdf) and a DocuSign link below. If you can have procurement sign the temp SOW (or submit the deposit) we will kick off infra provisioning and schedule the canary.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/temporary-sow/MX-2027-042
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-MX-2027-042

Please confirm whether procurement can sign the temp SOW or whether they need the deposit flow. If helpful, Karthik and I can join procurement's call to speed approvals.

— Monica
